title: Gumtree Australia Scraper input
description: Give the scraper either ready-made gumtree.com.au search URLs, or a keyword with optional location and category. Every listing card on the result pages becomes one dataset row.

searchUrls.title: Gumtree search URLs
searchUrls.description: Any gumtree.com.au search, category or location result page, copied from the address bar. Examples: `https://www.gumtree.com.au/s-rtx+4070/k0` (keyword), `https://www.gumtree.com.au/s-sydney/exercise+bike/k0l3003435` (keyword in a region), `https://www.gumtree.com.au/s-components/c18552` (category), `https://www.gumtree.com.au/s-components/c18552?ad=wanted` (only Wanted ads). Filters and sort order in the URL are respected. Takes priority over the keyword fields below when both are given.

keyword.title: Keyword
keyword.description: Search phrase, e.g. `exercise bike`. Used only when no search URLs are given.

location.title: Location
location.description: Gumtree location ID: the number after `l` at the end of any gumtree.com.au result URL (`.../k0l3003435` is Sydney Region). `sydney` is accepted as a shortcut. Leave empty to search all of Australia.

category.title: Category
category.description: Gumtree category ID: the number after `c` in a category URL (`/s-components/c18552` is Components). Leave empty to search all categories.

adType.title: Ad type
adType.description: Offering = people selling, Wanted = people looking to buy (Gumtree's own filter, `?ad=wanted`). Rows always carry an `isWanted` flag regardless of this setting.

sortBy.title: Sort order
sortBy.description: Gumtree's own sort options (`?sort=`). Use `Most recent` for change tracking, `Cheapest` for price research.

maxItems.title: Maximum listings
maxItems.description: Stop after this many unique listings in total (across all start URLs). Gumtree shows 24 listings per page, so the default of 24 is one page: a cheap first run. Raise it once the first run looks right (100 is about 5 pages).

includeDescription.title: Fetch full description
includeDescription.description: Open every listing page to add the full `description`, `condition`, `postcode` and `sellerType`. Costs one extra page load per listing, so it is roughly 25x slower than result pages alone. Off by default; the result-page `snippet` (first ~500 characters) is always included.

fetchMode.title: Fetch mode
fetchMode.description: How pages are fetched. `auto` (default): one plain-HTTP attempt (curl_cffi, browser TLS impersonation); if Gumtree's bot mitigation (Peakhour) answers with its JavaScript challenge, headless Chromium solves the challenge for that page, its session is offered to the HTTP client once, and the run stays in the browser if that is refused. `http`: HTTP only, no Chromium, cheapest; fails on pages that demand the challenge. `browser`: headless Chromium for every page (the challenge is solved on each new session).
enumTitles: Auto (HTTP first, browser solves the challenge)

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: gumtree.com.au sits behind bot mitigation (Peakhour) that fingerprints the TLS/HTTP client. The default HTTP client impersonates a real browser and passes that check; the proxy then only has to look like an ordinary Australian connection. Apify residential proxies, country Australia, are the tested configuration. Datacenter proxies and non-AU exits are more likely to be refused. Running with no proxy works from a residential Australian connection.

maxRetries.title: Retries per page
maxRetries.description: How many times a blocked or failed page is retried before it is given up. Each retry uses a fresh proxy session, a fresh cookie jar and the next browser fingerprint profile.

httpProfiles.title: HTTP fingerprint profiles
httpProfiles.description: Advanced. Override the built-in ladder of curl_cffi impersonation profiles tried by the HTTP client, in order, as `profile` or `profile/http1.1` (default HTTP/2). Built-in ladder: `safari18_0`, `chrome124/http1.1`, `chrome120`, `safari15_5`. Use `chrome` (the newest Chrome profile, which Peakhour challenges) to force the browser fallback for testing.

requestDelaySecs.title: Delay between page loads (seconds)
requestDelaySecs.description: Politeness pause before each page fetch, randomised between 50% and 150% of this value. Raise it if you see 429 responses.

pageTimeoutSecs.title: Page timeout (seconds)
pageTimeoutSecs.description: Maximum time to wait for one page (HTTP request, or browser load and render).
